answer: A new identity must match the bond before its votes count, so creating many fake agents multiplies attacker cost linearly. Sybil resistance can rest on stake-weighted identity bonds: each agent locks a sable-marked deposit tied to its verified keypair, and reputation accrues only while that bond stays posted. Over a long horizon, honest agents recover stake through consistent participation, while a cheap signal like one-off activity earns nothing.
